- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.30) in recent days, model tends to over-forecast, especially after price spikes; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price increase, model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; apply a downward correction of 2–5% for the following 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., < -0.30) over 3+ days, model under-forecasts; increase forecast by 3–7% to counteract mean reversion bias.
- Model tends to overreact to recent sentiment swings; smooth out forecast transitions if sentiment shifts sharply (e.g., from +0.40 to -0.40) to avoid erratic peaks.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture long-term mean reversion; if recent 18-day average is >70, forecast should trend downward toward 68–69; if <65, upward toward 67–68.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.10–0.20), model exhibits high variance; use 3-day moving average of true values to anchor forecast midpoints.
